clue.text: Be fathered illegitimately in luxurious place

indicators.note: done illegitimately means not done properly, so the letters before it are put out of their rightful order

blocks.note: the two words supply all ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A child of uncertain parentage is born into opulent surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Be fathered' rearrange to FEATHERBED, ten letters exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherbed is literally a soft mattress stuffed with plumes, and figuratively any situation of comfortable ease and pampering.

clue.text: Declines to rise around ceremony that's lively

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upwards, so the word is turned back to front
around says the turned word is split to wrap about the next piece

blocks.note: dips are falls or declines
a rite is a formal ceremony

explanation.surface: A market report: prices refuse to recover around some bustling ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: DIPS read upwards is SPID, which opens to take RITE: SPI-RITE-D.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirited describes someone full of energy, courage and vivacity, a close synonym of lively.

clue.text: Hollow metropolis embracing a victor

indicators.note: embracing means holding something in its arms, so the first word wraps around what follows

blocks.note: a metropolis is a large city
taken as written
V for victory or victor, as in V-sign

explanation.surface: A deserted city welcomes home its triumphant champion.
explanation.walkthrough: CITY takes A and V inside: C-AV-ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is an empty space inside something, which is what a hollow is as a noun.

clue.text: Nip absinthe regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the spirit's name

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick little drink of the green spirit now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: Nip in the surface is a small measure of spirits; here it is the verb meaning to bite.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip is to give a small sharp bite, as a dog or a crab does.

clue.text: Unquestionably from French (in a limited way)

blocks.note: de is the French word for from
something limited is finite, so acting this way is done finitely

explanation.surface: Someone insists, with a parenthetical caveat, that a claim certainly comes from the French.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make the phrase look like a hedge; it is the second half of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Definitely and unquestionably are adverbs both expressing certainty beyond any doubt.

clue.text: Mint drink is top

blocks.note: Polo is a British brand of mint sweet with a hole
in British slang to neck a drink is to gulp it down

explanation.surface: A review declaring a mint-flavoured beverage the best around.
explanation.walkthrough: Top looks like praise (the best) but is the garment. Polo mints are a British sweet; a polo neck is a sweater with a high folded collar (a turtleneck in the US).
explanation.definitionFit: A polo neck is a high-collared sweater, and top is the general word for a garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Pester and almost hurt fool

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word is cut short by its final letter

blocks.note: to hurt is to harm
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone bothers and nearly injures a simpleton.
explanation.walkthrough: Ass here is the everyday insult for a foolish person, not the donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To harass someone is to annoy or torment them persistently, which is what pestering does.

clue.text: Relinquish offspring reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: seed is an old word for descendants or offspring

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have given up their children.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed in the biblical sense means descendants, and it sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or a right is formally to give it up, which is to relinquish it.

clue.text: Impasse he cultivated, causing stress

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over and worked, so these letters are turned about into a new order

blocks.note: the two words supply all nine letters

explanation.surface: A man's carefully nurtured deadlock is making everyone anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: Stress in the surface is anxiety; as the definition it is the verb meaning to give weight to.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to give it special weight or prominence, which is to stress it.

clue.text: Love judge to hold forth

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
to rate something is to judge or assess it

explanation.surface: An instruction to love a judge enough to let them speak at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a long pompous speech, which is what holding forth means.

clue.text: Name I note for insect

blocks.note: a term is a name or word for something
taken as written
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone asks to identify a bug from a short memo.
explanation.definitionFit: A termite is a pale social insect that builds large mounds and eats wood, so it is a specific example.

clue.text: Keep apart from one getting very behind

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
so means very, as in so tired
behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: Advice to avoid a person who is chronically tardy.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate it and hold it away from others, the same as keeping it apart.

clue.text: Guard heading off for gate

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

blocks.note: a sentry is a soldier on guard

explanation.surface: A sentinel sets off to watch over an entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTRY without its first letter S leaves ENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a way in, and an entry is likewise a place of entrance or access.

clue.text: Save ruin crumbling and left for everyone to see

indicators.note: a crumbling structure falls apart into fragments that could be reassembled differently

blocks.note: eight of the nine letters to rearrange
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Conservationists plead to rescue a decaying ruin left on public view.
explanation.walkthrough: The L for left joins the rearranged letters of 'Save ruin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something universal applies to or is shared by all people, so it is open to everyone and anyone.

clue.text: Happy providing nurture

blocks.note: feeling up is feeling cheerful
bringing something is supplying or providing it

explanation.surface: A cheerful home that gives a child good care.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbringing is the care and training a child receives while growing, which is what nurture means as a noun.

clue.text: Books set on fire by English traitor you heard about

indicators.note: heard means taken by ear, so the pronoun is replaced by the letter that sounds the same

blocks.note: a fire that is set going is lit
E is the abbreviation for English
a rat is a betrayer or informer
the letter name is pronounced like the pronoun
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone tells you an English turncoat set fire to the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On fire' is not an anagram signal here: set on fire is simply LIT, and the remaining pieces follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature means written works collectively, especially novels, poems and plays, so books in general.

clue.text: Horribly bad end to holiday diet in guest house

indicators.note: something done horribly is badly messed up, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: six letters to rearrange
a break is a short holiday
to diet strictly is to fast

explanation.surface: A grim end to a holiday diet, suffered in a seaside guest house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End to' looks like a finishing signal but 'end' is part of the anagram fodder, and 'to' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed and breakfast is a small lodging offering a room for the night and a morning meal, much like a guest house.

clue.text: Pest lives in shade

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second, which opens to hold it

blocks.note: a nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or colour
lives here means exists, which is

explanation.surface: A bug that dwells somewhere in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: Shade is not darkness here but a fine distinction, as in a shade of meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or thing, and a nuisance is exactly that kind of irritant.

clue.text: Escort an eccentric old relative

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are knocked out of their usual places

blocks.note: the two words supply all eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to chaperone a quirky elderly family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric old relative' reads as one phrase about a dotty aunt, but 'eccentric' is the anagram signal and only 'old relative' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear from whom one is descended, a family member from generations long past.

clue.text: Sweet returns with legal end to currency fraud

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards
the end of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert
licit means lawful or permitted
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dessert comes back alongside a lawful conclusion to a money swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legal end' wants to be L, the last letter of legal; instead legal is LICIT whole and the end belongs to currency. Pud, short for pudding, is British for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Duplicity is deceitfulness or double-dealing, the deceptive behaviour that lies behind any fraud.

clue.text: Tart old line?

blocks.note: past means former or old
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued question about a stale chat-up line.
explanation.walkthrough: Tart reads as an adjective meaning sharp; it is the noun, a baked dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart is an open baked case of dough with a filling, and pastry is the dough it is made from or such baked goods generally.

clue.text: Discover crude Corsican ornament

indicators.note: to discover is to uncover something already present, so the letters lie within the next words

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone unearths a rough piece of Corsican decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the last two letters of 'crude' and first three of 'Corsican'.
explanation.definitionFit: Decor is the decoration and furnishing of a room, and ornament is decoration collectively.

clue.text: Ends in outhouse overturned, holding a toilet's lid

indicators.note: something overturned is upended, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom upwards
a lid sits on top, so only the topmost letter of the word is kept
holding means grasping inside, so the turned word wraps around the other pieces

blocks.note: a shed is an outbuilding
taken as written
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Tragic ends in a toppled outdoor privy, with the seat still on.
explanation.walkthrough: An outhouse is normally an outdoor toilet, which feeds the surface; in the wordplay it is any small outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A death is the end of a life, so deaths are ends in the grim, final sense.

clue.text: Wild horse has to enrage without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation sound is removed from the word

blocks.note: if you have to do something, you must
to enrage someone is to anger them
er is the sound of a hesitating speaker

explanation.surface: A bronco is bound to infuriate, and does so without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without hesitation' reads as 'promptly', but it tells you to drop the hesitation sound from the word before.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a free-roaming feral horse of the American West, a specific kind of wild horse.

clue.text: Bloke held up by little lamb

indicators.note: held means contained, so the letters are inside the following words
in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A man is delayed by a small sheep in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Held up looks like delayed; it splits into a containment signal and an upward reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloke is British slang for a man, and male is the noun for a man or boy.

clue.text: Journey from property crossing middle of Kansas

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letters, here the two at its heart
crossing means straddling, so the first word spans across the other piece

blocks.note: a trait is a characteristic or property
the central two letters of the state name

explanation.surface: A trip starting from a ranch and going across the prairie state.
explanation.walkthrough: Property looks like land or real estate; it means a characteristic.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is passage from one place to another, so it means a journey or the act of travelling.

clue.text: Time to be sickly comes to an end

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: A period of illness finally draws to a close.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail is the rear or last part of something, as in the tail of a queue, so its end.

clue.text: Emotional lines you recited invoked confusion initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the leading letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Reciting heartfelt verses caused bewilderment among the listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emotional lines' wants to be the definition as a song's words, but lines starts the wordplay and only Emotional defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poetry expresses the writer's personal feelings, so as an adjective lyric means expressing strong emotion.

clue.text: Huge robin performing for someone nearby

indicators.note: performers act out a routine, so these letters are put through their paces into a new order

blocks.note: the two words supply all nine letters

explanation.surface: An enormous bird is putting on a show for a person close by.
explanation.definitionFit: A neighbour is a person living next door or close at hand, so somebody located near you.
